name: Bhawana Aryal
tagline: Architect · Urban Design & Research · Kathmandu, Nepal
heroStatement: I'm curious about how small spaces bring people together — and how better streets and public spaces can make cities healthier and more inclusive for everyone.
shortBio: Architecture graduate from the Institute of Engineering, Thapathali Campus, now working as an Architect at Impulse Consultant in Kathmandu. Winner of the Cities for Women International Urban Design Competition 2025, and a USYC 2026 cohort member. My work moves between architecture, urban design and research — always coming back to people and the everyday life of spaces.
aboutIntro: My interest in architecture began with simple observations — the way a small space can unite people, and the influence a neighborhood has on day-to-day life. Those observations taught me that architecture is not really about buildings; it is about the spaces in which people live and connect.
aboutBody:
Over the past five years I have grown through design studios, research fieldwork, competitions and practice. I am especially drawn to urban planning and design — to how better streets and public spaces can make cities healthier and more inclusive. Alongside design work, I research settlement patterns, accessibility and the 15-minute city, and I love documenting places through maps, sketches and photographs.

Outside the studio you will find me travelling, taking photographs, organising events, and writing about the places and people I meet along the way.
philosophy: Architecture is not about the buildings — it is about the spaces in which people themselves can live and connect.

usyc.title: USYC 2026 Cohort Member
usyc.text: Currently part of the USYC 2026 cohort — a journey of leadership, learning and exchange with young changemakers. Reflections and experiences from the cohort will be shared in the journal.

timeline.title: Bachelor of Architecture, Tribhuvan University
